If you’ve been thinking about selling digital products but don’t know what to create, save this post! 👇 You don’t need to spend months trying to figure everything out. You need a simple process that takes you from IDEA ➡️ PRODUCT ➡️ STOREFRONT ➡️ MARKETING. Here are 6 ChatGPT prompts you can copy and paste to help you get started. ⚫ PROMPT 1: FIND A PROFITABLE PRODUCT IDEA “Act as a digital product strategist. Give me 20 beginner-friendly digital product ideas I can create using Canva. Focus on problems people are actively trying to solve. For each idea, identify the target audience, the problem it solves, a suggested selling price, and why someone might purchase it.” ⚫ PROMPT 2: CREATE THE PRODUCT CONTENT “I want to create a [digital product] for [target audience]. Help me develop the complete content, including the title, sections, instructions, worksheets, and any additional information that would make this product useful. Organize everything so I can easily transfer it into Canva.” ⚫ PROMPT 3: DESIGN YOUR PRODUCT IN CANVA “Act as a professional digital product designer. Help me create a design plan for my [digital product]. Recommend a color palette, fonts, page layout, visual elements, and Canva template search terms. Make the design clean, professional, and appealing to my target audience.” ⚫ PROMPT 4: CREATE YOUR SALES PAGE “Act as a conversion copywriter. Write a compelling product description for my [digital product]. Include an attention-grabbing headline, the problem it solves, key benefits, what’s included, and a clear call to action. Make it suitable for a Stan Store product listing.” ⚫ PROMPT 5: ATTRACT POTENTIAL CUSTOMERS “Act as a TikTok content strategist. Create 15 short-form video ideas to promote my [digital product]. Include curiosity-driven hooks, educational captions, and calls to action. Focus on attracting beginners who would benefit from my product without making unrealistic income claims.” ⚫ PROMPT 6: CREATE A 7-DAY MARKETING PLAN “Create a beginner-friendly 7-day marketing plan for launching my [digital product]. Include daily TikTok content ideas, ways to build trust with my audience, engagement strategies, and methods for directing interested viewers to my Stan Store.” ⸻ 💡 HERE’S THE PART MOST BEGINNERS OVERLOOK. Creating a digital product is only half the process. You still need to get people to see it. That’s where digital marketing comes in. You can use ChatGPT to develop the content, Canva to design the product, and Stan Store to sell it. Then use platforms like TikTok to attract people who might actually need what you’ve created. And remember: You don’t need 40 products to get started. You need ONE useful product that solves ONE specific problem for ONE specific audience. Start there. ‼️ Follow me and turn on notifications. What exactly IS a digital product? Let me break down every type — with examples. If you've been seeing people talk about 'selling digital products' and wondering what they're actually selling — this is for you. A digital product is anything you create once and sell repeatedly — delivered instantly online, no shipping, no inventory, no returns. Here are the main types: 📄 EBOOKS & GUIDES — PDFs that teach something specific. 'Beginner's Guide to Instagram,' '30-Day Content Plan,' 'How to Start Affiliate Marketing.' Sell for $7–$47. Create in Canva for free. 🎨 TEMPLATES — Pre-made designs buyers customize. Instagram templates, planners, resumes, business cards. Sell for $9–$97. Create in Canva. 🎓 COURSES & WORKSHOPS — Video or written lessons teaching a skill. Can sell for $47–$997+. Host on Stan Store or Beacons. 📦 DONE-FOR-YOU PRODUCTS (PLR/MRR) — Products already created that you can resell. Perfect for beginners who aren't ready to create from scratch yet. 📋 PLANNERS, WORKBOOKS & PRINTABLES — Fillable or printable pages. Budget planners, habit trackers, goal workbooks. Sell for $5–$37. These get the most saves and shares on social. The best part? You don't have to create anything to start. You can begin with a done-for-you product while you're still learning — then create your own once you understand what your audience actually wants. Save this. Share it with someone who's been confused about what this is.
